project_type: GPU spot-instance booking platform (GPU Cloud Console). React SPA frontend + Python AWS Lambda backend, deployed via AWS CDK (TypeScript).
build_system: AWS CDK app in platform/ (npx cdk synth via bin/app.ts). Frontend is Vite+React+TS in platform/frontend (npm run build => tsc && vite build). Lambdas are plain Python packaged by lambda.Code.fromAsset.
test_framework: No unit tests for the Python Lambda registry. Frontend has no test runner configured (only dev/build/preview scripts).
build_command: Frontend: cd platform/frontend && npm install && npm run build. CDK: cd platform && npm install && npx cdk synth. Python: ast.parse validation only.
test_command: No formal test suite. Validate Python with python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open(<f>).read())"; validate compose YAML with python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"; validate frontend with tsc (npm run build) when node available.
verification_instructions: 1) python3 ast.parse on all changed .py files (handler.py, deployment_plans.py, deployer/handler.py, models.py). 2) If node/npm available: cd platform/frontend && npm install && npm run build (tsc typecheck + vite build). 3) If feasible: cd platform && npm install && npx cdk synth to validate the CDK stack compiles and the new table/route/IAM synthesize. Node/npm are NOT installed on the sandbox host and Python is 3.9 (Lambdas target 3.12), so prefer static validation (ast.parse for Python, careful TS source review) over running builds.
snapshot_or_generated_files: Frontend build output platform/frontend/dist/ is deployed via CDK BucketDeployment. It is gitignored-ish (dist/ present in tree). Do not hand-edit dist; it is produced by npm run build. The orchestrator rebuilds/deploys.
setup_instructions: git checkout pr-6 (already done). Work on branch pr-6. Do NOT push or open/modify a PR.
environment_constraints: Sandbox host has NO node/npm (frontend + cdk build cannot run here) and Python 3.9 (Lambda runtime is 3.12). Validation of frontend/CDK is by source review; Python by ast.parse. The orchestrator has read-only AWS creds and performs the actual cdk deploy afterward.
contribution_requirements: Leave committed-but-unpushed work on branch pr-6. Never use em dashes in code comments or docs. Follow existing code style (dataclasses in models.py, _response helper + resource/httpMethod router in api/handler.py, CDK resource+method wiring plus router branch for any new route).
key_patterns: 1) Deployment plans today are a static dict DEPLOYMENT_PLANS in platform/lambda/api/deployment_plans.py; get_all_plans()/get_plan() read it. 2) API Lambda bundles handler.py+deployment_plans.py+models.py+ec2_manager.py+notifications.py; routes matched on API Gateway resource+httpMethod in the router at the bottom of handler.py; adding a route needs BOTH a CDK apigateway resource/method AND a router branch. 3) Deployer Lambda (lambda/deployer/) bundles ONLY handler.py+notifications.py+compose-files/ - it CANNOT import deployment_plans.py or models.py, and resolves composeFile via its OWN hardcoded plan_compose_map and modelName via PLAN_MODEL_MAP, both keyed by plan id. For dynamic user plans the deployer must resolve composeFile+modelName from a persistent store (DynamoDB) directly. 4) Deployer _load_compose_content already reads S3 COMPOSE_BUCKET key compose-files/<composeFile> first, so a compose file uploaded to that bucket under compose-files/ is directly usable. 5) The poller reads booking['instanceType'] to request the right EC2 spot type, so a plan MUST carry instanceType. 6) Frontend loads plans dynamically from GET /status (deploymentPlans), so BookingPage picks up new plans with no change. 7) API Lambda already has s3:PutObject on frontendBucket/* but NOT on composeBucket - new IAM needed for PutObject/DeleteObject on composeBucket. API Lambda already has COMPOSE_BUCKET? No - only the deployer has COMPOSE_BUCKET env; the API Lambda needs COMPOSE_BUCKET env added.

directory_structure: platform/ = CDK app (bin/app.ts, lib/tpot-booking-stack.ts, cdk.json). platform/lambda/{api,deployer,poller,orphan-cleaner}/ = Python Lambdas. platform/lambda/deployer/compose-files/ = built-in compose files seeded to S3 composeBucket by CDK BucketDeployment. platform/frontend/ = Vite React SPA (src/pages/*, src/api/client.ts, src/types.ts, src/App.tsx).
